inputs.root_cause: SAL-NRRD-OBL-4CAFF21A47F62F19 (NRRD-PAYLOAD-001) requires distinguishing pre-NRRD0004 leading-./ detached-path rules from NRRD0004+ relative-path rules. reader.py's _safe_detached_payload and lazy.py's _resolve_detached_path both applied the NRRD0004+ rule unconditionally regardless of declared version, confirmed by reading both functions directly (neither branches on version at all before this slice).
inputs.acceptance_evidence: Both reader.py and lazy.py now branch on version < 4: a leading './' prefix is recognized and stripped (header-relative, matching pre-NRRD0004 semantics), while a bare relative name without './' is refused with a clear error rather than silently resolved as header-relative (the NRRD0004+ rule) -- strict spec semantics define this case as cwd-relative, an unconfined resolution base this reader deliberately does not support without an explicit caller-supplied resolver policy (SAL-NRRD-OBL-09CDF5A28C011CD7's own remaining, honestly-declared gap). 12 new tests across 2 files prove all 4 version/prefix combinations plus confirm directory confinement still holds after the prefix-stripping change.
inputs.regression_tier: full nrrd package suite (tests/python/nrrd) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Read the pinned spec source directly (.local/format-contracts/acquired/nrrd/src-nrrd-001.bin, SRC-NRRD-001): confirmed verbatim 'as of NRRD0004, the signifier of a header-relative file changed from the presence (at the beginning of the filename) of "./", to the absence of "/" ... With this change, it becomes impossible for a header to refer to the data file relative to the current working directory of the reader' -- establishing precisely that pre-NRRD0004 bare-relative names are cwd-relative, a genuinely different (and more permissive/dangerous) resolution base than header-relative.

2. Read reader.py's _safe_detached_payload and lazy.py's _resolve_detached_path directly: both apply the NRRD0004+ rule (no leading '/' means header-relative) unconditionally, confirming the version-blindness is real, not a stale citation.

3. Considered implementing genuine unconfined cwd-relative resolution for the pre-NRRD0004 bare-relative case (strict spec literalism) but declined: this reader's own established security discipline (directory-confinement checks already present in both functions) has no natural confinement boundary for cwd-relative resolution, and introducing it unconditionally would be a security regression relative to this session's SEC-001 discipline. Chose instead to refuse the case explicitly with a clear error, leaving the caller-supplied-resolver-policy half of the obligation cluster (SAL-NRRD-OBL-09CDF5A28C011CD7) honestly partial rather than rushing an opt-in mechanism.

4. Implemented the version < 4 branch in both reader.py and lazy.py identically: './' prefix recognized and stripped, bare-relative names refused with an explanatory NrrdParseError. Threaded `version` through both call sites (reader.py's _load already had it from _parse_header; lazy.py's NrrdHeader dataclass already exposed .version).

5. Verified interactively before writing any test: NRRD0003 with './' resolves, NRRD0003 without './' is refused, NRRD0004/NRRD0005 without './' resolve (unchanged), NRRD0004/NRRD0005 with './' still resolve (not rejected) -- all 4 cases correct on the first attempt.

6. Wrote 11 new tests in a new file (reader.py path) plus 1 new test in the existing lazy-payload-access test file (lazy.py's duplicated resolution logic, proven separately so the two code paths cannot silently diverge). Ran ruff (clean) and the full nrrd suite (512 passed, was 500, +12) before writing any evidence claim. Ran the full 6-format regression (3051 passed, was 3039, +12; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.
